transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably just me being a bit silly, but... well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

I don't want you to think I keep a messy house—I really do try my best to keep things nice—but right now, my kitchen table is just completely covered. It's got all my husband’s medical appointment papers, and flyers from church, and little notes from the senior center, plus all these half-finished to-do lists I keep making. I just sit there looking at it all, and I honestly don't know which thing I'm supposed to do first. And then, before I know it, the whole day is just gone and I haven't done any of it. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Did you have similar difficulties with focus, organization, or completing tasks when you were a child?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose I did. I always wanted to be a good student, I really did, but... well, my mother kept all my old report cards, and I'm a little embarrassed to say it, but the teachers usually wrote that I was a bright little girl, but... careless. That was the word they always used. 

I didn't mean to be, of course! But I was just always forgetting my books, or leaving my homework behind. And, um, they constantly had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside to play. I'd just sit there and get so lost in my own little world instead of finishing my papers. 

Is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope I don't sound like I was a terrible child, Doctor, I really did try my best to be good and do what I was told.
Have these difficulties gotten noticeably worse in the past year or two?

Well, I... I hate to admit it, because I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or just making excuses. But... yes, I suppose it really has gotten quite a bit worse lately. I'd say it's been causing me this much trouble for, oh, about a year and three months now? 

That was right around the time my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and his daily arrangements. I really do try my absolute best to keep everything perfectly organized for him, because he's such a dear and he really needs me, but... well, it's just gotten so difficult for me to keep track of it all. I feel just terrible that I can't seem to manage his schedule the way a good wife should. 

I hope you don't think poorly of me for having such a hard time with it... does that sound like an understandable reason to be struggling?
Before this got worse, did anything stressful or upsetting happen in your life?

Oh... well, I've tried to think about that, and... no, not really. I mean, nothing terrible or upsetting happened before that. We've been very blessed, honestly. 

Aside from my husband just getting a bit older and needing more of my help—which is perfectly natural, of course—there weren't any big tragedies or sudden shocks. I almost feel a little silly, like I ought to have a better excuse for why I'm suddenly struggling so much. I hope it's alright that I don't have a... a real reason, like a trauma or something. I just, I don't know why I can't keep up when everything else in my life has been perfectly fine. 

Is it okay that nothing else happened? I hope I'm giving you the right kinds of answers.
In the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I haven't been feeling sad or down like that. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself when I forget things, of course, but... overall, I'm quite a cheerful person! 

I really try to count my blessings and look on the bright side. I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around moping all day. I have so much to be thankful for, and I try to keep a smile on my face for my husband. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm too cheerful when I'm supposed to be here for a problem, but I really haven't been feeling depressed or anything like that.
Have you ever had a stroke, head injury, or other brain illness?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that. I've always been very healthy, thankfully. No strokes or... or head injuries, or anything scary like that. 

I've always tried to take very good care of myself, you know, eating right and staying active, so I wouldn't be a burden to anyone. I hope that's a good thing to hear? I'd hate to think I'm wasting your time when my brain is otherwise perfectly healthy... it's just this silly forgetfulness and trouble focusing that's bothering me. Is that alright?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy my little hobbies and things. I mean, I love working in my garden and doing my crosswords... 

I will admit, sometimes I don't quite finish them like I used to, or I get a bit distracted and leave my gardening tools out, but... I still enjoy doing them! I really do. I haven't lost interest at all. I just... well, maybe I don't get as much done as I'd like. But the joy is still there! 

I hope that's the right answer. I just want to be clear that I still love my life and my activities, even if I'm a bit scatterbrained lately. Is that what you meant?
Do you have these attention and organization problems in more than one part of your life, such as at home and in other settings too?

Well, I suppose... yes, it does happen in a few different places. I try so hard to keep everything running smoothly at home, I really do. But... well, my daughter has started double-checking my bills and my appointments. She says she just wants to help, but I know it's because she doesn't quite trust me to keep everything straight on my own anymore. I hate making her worry like that. 

And, oh, I feel terrible even bringing this up, but... I actually had to step down from leading this big event we put on at the senior center. I just couldn't keep all the details organized, and I didn't want to let everyone down. I hope you don't think less of me for that. I always prided myself on being so capable, you know? It's just a little embarrassing to admit I can't juggle it all like I used to. Does that answer your question alright?
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to sit still?

Oh, no, not really. I'm actually quite content just... sitting quietly. I don't get fidgety or feel like I need to be up and moving all the time. 

I mean, I might shift in my chair now and then to get comfortable, like anyone would, but I don't feel restless inside. I'm perfectly happy just resting or reading a book, even if my mind wanders a bit. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I don't want you to think I'm hyperactive or anything like that. I'm really quite calm, physically, at least. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed your memory or thinking getting worse overall, beyond just the trouble with organization and focus?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think so, anyway. I mean, my memory itself is still quite sharp, thank goodness! I can remember all my grandchildren's birthdays and things that happened years ago just fine. It's really just... well, like I said, those scatterbrained moments. I might forget where I set my gardening gloves down, but I think that's just because I wasn't paying attention when I did it, you know? Not because my mind is actually failing. 

I hope I'm explaining the difference properly. I know at my age, people start to worry about... well, the really scary memory problems. But I honestly feel like my thinking is still perfectly clear, just a little... cluttered sometimes when I try to do too much. Is that a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory or thinking has changed compared with a year or two ago?

Oh, no, I don't believe so. My daughter—bless her heart, she keeps such a close eye on me—she hasn't said anything about my actual memory changing, no. Not compared to a year or two ago, anyway. 

She knows I've always been a little... well, easily distracted, I suppose. But she hasn't mentioned any new problems with my thinking. I think she knows my mind is still perfectly sound, just a bit disorganized sometimes. 

I hope that's reassuring to hear? I really try my best to stay sharp, so I certainly hope no one thinks I'm slipping in that way. I'd hate to be a burden like that. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that. I've always needed my rest, and I certainly don't get these... bursts of wild energy or anything. I usually try to get my full eight hours every night, just like a sensible person should. 

I mean, there are days when I might wake up feeling a bit more refreshed and get a lot done around the house, but that's just a good day, right? Not anything unusual or... extreme. I definitely wouldn't say I've gone days without needing sleep. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure you know I'm very steady in that regard. I wouldn't want you to think I was behaving erratically. Does that sound normal to you?
Before the past year or so, did these attention and organization problems cause you similar trouble throughout your adult life?

Well, yes... I suppose if I'm being perfectly honest, it's been that way for a very long time. Not just my adult life, really. 

Even way back when I was a little girl... oh, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but my teachers always used to write on my report cards that I was bright—which was very sweet of them to say!—but they'd always add that I was, well, careless. I was always forgetting my reading books or my homework. And they'd have to give me so many reminders to just finish my seatwork before I could go outside to play with the others. 

I just always had my head in the clouds, I suppose. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly irresponsible? I really have always tried my best to do things properly, I just... well, my mind likes to wander. Is that the sort of background information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you a good picture of things.
